title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 'variations on the loop equation' in the Longue Marche notes. Grothendieck is studying the conjugation or commutator maps attached to the torsion elements of SL(2,Z). One is the order-3 element ρ, with A_ρ = A[ρ] ≅ A[x]/(x²+x+1). The other is the order-4 element σ, with A_σ = A[σ] ≅ A[i]. Both are taken over a base S = Spec A.

The question is when a matrix ξ (respectively η) that locally has the right shape is globally of the form βρβ⁻¹ (or [β,σ]) with β in SL(2,A). The previous page found the answer. Locally, β exists in GL(2,A), with a Pic(A_ρ)-type obstruction to doing it globally. Upgrading β to SL(2) requires det α to lie in N_{A_ρ/A}(A_ρ*). So the residual obstruction lives in A*/N(A_ρ*). By local class field theory, for A = Z_ℓ this group is trivial except at ℓ = 3, where it is Z/2 (Z_3[ω]/Z_3 is ramified and the norm group from units has index 2).

Order-3 case (23). For α = (a b; c d), an explicit computation gives (ad−bc)·D = c²+cd+d², where D is an entry of the target matrix ξ. The right-hand side is N(cρ+d). Hence D is invertible iff cρ+d ∈ A_ρ*, and then det α = N(cρ+d)/D. Since norms of units from Z_3[ω] are ≡ 1 mod 3, the class of det α in Z_3*/N ≅ ±1 is read off from D mod 3. In other words, the ℓ = 3 obstruction is the residue of D mod 3.

Parenthetical check. Can D ≡ 0 mod 3? Reducing mod 3, ξ = (A B; 1+B 0) with −B(1+B) = 1, i.e. B²+B+1 = 0. Over F_3 this is (B−1)² = 0, so B = 1. (He first wrote B = 0 or −1, then crossed it out and argued via B³ = 1 in characteristic 3.) Thus ξ = (A 1; −1 0), and ξρ is upper triangular unipotent up to sign. It is 'singular' (i.e. regular, non-scalar) iff A ≠ −1. So D ≡ 0 mod 3 cannot be excluded a priori.

Order-4 case (24)–(31). Take σ = (0 −1; 1 0), with σ⁴ = 1 and σ² = −1. Then A_σ = Z[i] for A = Z, and Pic(Z[i]) is trivial (class number 1). The image of β ↦ βσβ⁻¹σ⁻¹ must satisfy det η = 1 and Tr(ησ) = Tr σ = 0, i.e. η is symmetric (continued on the next page). Over Z, the remaining obstruction to taking β ∈ SL(2,Z) is Z*/N(Z[i]*) = ±1. This matches the relation (rt−su)U = t²+u² = N(tσ+u). Concretely, for β ∈ SL2, η = ββᵀ is positive definite, so symmetric η with negative diagonal are not hit.

This is the classical link between sums of two squares or three-term norm forms, Z[i] and Z[ω], and binary quadratic forms, rephrased as a torsor/descent obstruction computation.
errors: The marginal claim 'c²+cd+d² ≡ 1 (3)' is not true in general. Norms from Z[ω] are ≡ 0 or 1 mod 3. The claim holds only when cρ+d is a unit (or prime to 1−ω), which is the case assumed here.
Over A = Z, c²+cd+d² is positive definite. So 'invertible' forces N = 1 and D = ±1, and the sign statement is trivial. The mod-3 argument is really meaningful over Z_3 or more general A.
The crossed-out solution 'B = 0 or B = −1' of B²+B+1 = 0 over F_3 is wrong. The correct root is the double root B = 1, which Grothendieck fixes.
'singulière ssi A ≠ −1' should presumably read 'non-scalar/regular'. The sign conventions in the product ξρ depend on the choice of ρ and do not exactly match the displayed result.

ideas.what: Obstruction to writing ξ = βρβ⁻¹ with β ∈ SL2 rather than GL2 lies in A*/N_{A_ρ/A}(A_ρ*); for Z_3 it is ±1 and is detected by D mod 3
ideas.modern_name: Norm-residue obstruction / conjugacy classes of torsion in SL2 over rings (Latimer–MacDuffee, descent with torus stabilizer)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Latimer–MacDuffee–Taussky (classes ↔ ideals); local class field theory

ideas.what: Matrices in the image of β ↦ [β,σ] for σ of order 4 are exactly the symmetric matrices of det 1, up to a ±1 norm obstruction; Pic(Z[i]) is trivial
ideas.modern_name: Representation of symmetric unimodular matrices as ββᵀ / sums of two squares via Z[i]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss, classical reduction theory of binary forms

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine explicit calculations of classical norm and conjugacy obstructions for the torsion elements of SL(2,Z), in service of the loop-equation study. There is nothing beyond known results.
transcription_corrections: '(25) Pic(A_σ) = 10' is most likely 'Pic(A_σ) = 1' (or 0), i.e. trivial; the class number of Z[i] is 1.
'(b.f. Kervaire)' is doubtful; the parenthetical after 'on a encore' is illegible and probably not 'Kervaire'.
The crossed-out text after B²+B+1 = 0 reads 'i.e. B = 0 ou B = −1', and is replaced by 'donc B³ = 1 donc (car 3) B = 1'.
Margin: 'car c²+cd+d² ≡ 1 (3)' (the first character is 'car', with c² overwritten).
